To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reliability of waste quantification studies is hard to verify, the convergence rule should be adopted to identify the most likely figures, and the platform for reporting false or dubious citation should be set up.

the reliability of waste quantification and projections can be improved by adopting a prudent approach to data collection and citation, and by establishing an academic platform to monitor and report false citations.

(1) the best method of waste quantification is to use the convergence rule, (2) the transparency of data reporting in academic studies is not high, and (3) a citation platform for academic studies should be established.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reliability of the data and the methods of quantification.
the reliability and validity of the waste quantity data and the methods used for its estimation.
the quality of data and the quality of research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current waste quantification and projections of e-waste in mainland China are not reliable.
the current state of e-waste studies in mainland China does not allow for the establishment of an accurate e-waste generation projection.
waste quantification is a complex and difficult task and the results of such studies should be interpreted cautiously.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best waste quantifying method should be the one with the most transparent data collection and computation method and the least number of false citations.
the best way to estimate the quantity of waste is to use the most recent, transparently reported and meticulously computed data.
the reliability of e-waste quantifications is not satisfactory, and that the reliability of future e-waste quantitations should be improved.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to improve the reliability of e-waste quantifications, more effort needs to be made on improving the transparency and quality of the studies, and on reducing irresponsible citation practices.
the reliability of the waste quantity data can be improved through the adoption of the convergence rule.
waste quantification and projections are difficult and should be treated with great care.
